title: What shapes can the shadow of a cube make?
description: A cube is turned in front of a light, and the board follows its shadow. A face held straight on gives a square, a cube turned about one edge gives a rectangle, and a cube with three faces showing gives a hexagon.
teaching_notes: One idea: the shape of the shadow depends on how many faces of the cube show. Watch for students who think a cube can only cast a square.

source: Figure it Out (shadows and views, question 6)
video_script.why: The child lists the shapes the shadow of a cube can take by turning the cube and counting the faces that show.
video_script.substitution: Turn the cube, count the faces that show, and name the outline of the shadow.
video_script.anchor: a cube that can be turned in front of a torch, with a screen behind it that shows the shadow
video_script.payoff_line: The shadow of a cube can be a square, a rectangle or a hexagon

final_answer.value: A square, a rectangle or a hexagon
final_answer.spoken: a square, a rectangle or a hexagon

hold_back: Answer: a square, a rectangle or a hexagon
never_show: a circle or a triangle marked as a shadow of a cube
maths_rules: one face straight on to the screen: the shadow is a square
turned about one edge, two faces show: the shadow is a rectangle
three faces show: the shadow is a hexagon, with six equal sides when the cube balances on a corner
a cube shows one, two or three faces at a time
video_script.design: A cube turns slowly in front of a torch. The screen shows its shadow, and the visible faces are tinted one at a time as the shape changes from a square to a rectangle to a hexagon.
